notes_for_adoption: This taxonomy categorizes content themes known for high user retention and 'addictive' properties. Use 'psychological_driver' for educational tooltips and 'warnings' for content linters.

process_and_completion.name: Process & Completion
process_and_completion.description: Themes that tap into the human desire to see a task through from start to finish, providing a dopamine hit upon completion ('order from chaos').

themes.name: Transformation & Renovation
themes.description: Following a long-term project (home, car, furniture) from a 'bad' state to a 'good' one. Includes 'flipping' content.
examples: Abandoned Project Car Gets a Full Restoration
themes.psychological_driver: Satisfies the desire for problem-solving, visual progress, and a dramatic final reveal.
warnings: Sets unrealistic expectations for time, cost, and effort in real life.
Can promote dissatisfaction with one's own environment.

themes.name: Restoration & Cleaning
themes.description: Videos showing 'order from chaos' in a short loop. Power washing, car detailing, 'clean with me,' decluttering, etc.
themes.psychological_driver: A pure, fast, and visually 'satisfying' hit of completion and order without any physical effort from the viewer.
warnings: Can be fetishized, potentially contributing to obsessive-compulsive thoughts.
Sets unrealistic standards of cleanliness.

themes.name: Creation Process
themes.description: Watching a skilled artisan or creator make something from scratch (art, food, craft, code).
examples: How I Paint a Photorealistic Portrait
Building a Video Game in 100 Days
themes.psychological_driver: Combines the satisfaction of completion with admiration for skill ('flow state') and a sense of vicarious achievement.
warnings: Can be discouraging to beginners who compare their 'messy' process to the curated final product.

social_and_parasocial.name: Social & Parasocial
social_and_parasocial.description: Themes that tap into the human need for social connection, status, and drama. Creates a 'parasocial' (one-sided) relationship with the creator.

themes.name: Interpersonal Drama
themes.description: Following ongoing conflicts, relationship updates, or controversies involving creators or public figures.
themes.psychological_driver: Satisfies curiosity about social dynamics and provides a sense of 'insider' knowledge. Triggers the same neural pathways as real-life gossip.
warnings: Promotes negativity and voyeurism.
Can normalize toxic behavior and conflict.
May spread misinformation.

themes.name: Daily Vlog / Lifestyle
themes.description: Following someone's daily life, creating a parasocial relationship where the viewer feels like a 'friend'.
examples: A Day in My Life as a...
themes.psychological_driver: Creates a false sense of intimacy and friendship. The brain processes it similarly to real social interaction.
regex_triggers: /(day in my life|come with me|weekly vlog|daily vlog)/i
/(morning routine|night routine|what i eat in a day)/i
warnings: Can lead to unhealthy parasocial attachments.
May create unrealistic lifestyle expectations.
Viewer may neglect real-life relationships.

themes.name: Reaction & Commentary
themes.description: Watching someone else react to or comment on other content, providing a 'shared viewing experience'.
themes.psychological_driver: Provides social context and validation for the viewer's own opinions. Reduces loneliness by simulating 'watching together'.
warnings: Can be intellectually lazy; viewer consumes opinions rather than forming their own.
May amplify negativity if the reaction is critical.

novelty_and_unboxing.name: Novelty & Unboxing
novelty_and_unboxing.description: Themes that tap into the dopamine hit of discovering something new or witnessing a 'reveal'.

themes.name: Unboxing / Haul
themes.description: Watching someone open and display new products or purchases.
themes.psychological_driver: Triggers the same dopamine response as making a purchase yourself, without the cost. Satisfies curiosity about new products.
warnings: Promotes consumerism and impulse buying.
Can lead to dissatisfaction with one's own possessions.
Often includes undisclosed sponsorships.

themes.name: Try-On / Taste Test
themes.description: Watching someone try new products, foods, or experiences for the first time.
themes.psychological_driver: Vicarious novelty. The viewer experiences the 'new' thing through the creator, satisfying curiosity without risk.
warnings: Can promote overconsumption and waste.
May create FOMO (fear of missing out).

themes.name: Trend Participation
themes.description: Content that participates in a viral trend, challenge, or meme format.
themes.psychological_driver: Combines novelty with social proof. The viewer wants to be 'in the know' and part of the cultural moment.
warnings: Extremely short lifespan; quickly becomes irrelevant.
Can promote dangerous challenges.
Often low-effort content.

low_cognitive_load.name: Low Cognitive Load
low_cognitive_load.description: Content that requires minimal mental effort to consume, allowing for 'mindless scrolling' and dissociation.

themes.name: Brainrot / Sludge Content
themes.description: Multi-layered content with unrelated, high-stimulation elements playing simultaneously (e.g., gameplay footage with a podcast voiceover and subtitles from a different video).
themes.psychological_driver: Overstimulates the brain to the point of dissociation. Each element individually is not engaging enough, but together they trap attention.
warnings: Reduces attention span and ability to focus on single-task content.
Can lead to dissociative states and time loss.
Highly addictive.
themes.notes_for_devs: Extremely difficult to detect programmatically without advanced video analysis.

themes.name: Compilation / Loop
themes.description: Short, repetitive clips compiled together or a single action looped endlessly.
themes.psychological_driver: Each clip is short enough that the brain never fully 'checks out.' The promise of a 'better' clip keeps the viewer watching.
warnings: Can lead to long viewing sessions with no memory of what was watched.
Reduces ability to engage with longer-form content.

themes.name: Shorts / Feed Scrolling
themes.description: The act of endlessly scrolling through a feed of short-form vertical videos (TikTok, YouTube Shorts, Instagram Reels).
themes.psychological_driver: Variable reward schedule. Each swipe might reveal something interesting, triggering the same neural pathways as slot machines.
warnings: Extremely addictive due to variable reward and low barrier to next video.
Can lead to hours of lost time.
Difficult to moderate at the individual video level; the feed itself is the problem.
themes.notes_for_devs: This is a platform-level pattern, not a content pattern. Detection would focus on the user's scrolling behavior, not the content itself.

aspirational_envy.name: Aspirational & Envy
aspirational_envy.description: Themes that showcase wealth, success, beauty, or lifestyle that the viewer aspires to but likely cannot attain, creating a mix of inspiration and dissatisfaction.

themes.name: Luxury & Lifestyle
themes.description: Content showcasing expensive products, travel, homes, or experiences.
examples: A Day in My Life as a Millionaire
themes.psychological_driver: Triggers both aspiration and envy. The viewer fantasizes about the lifestyle while potentially feeling inadequate about their own.
warnings: Can foster materialism and dissatisfaction.
May promote unrealistic financial goals.
Often obscures the actual cost or privilege involved.

themes.name: Aesthetic & Inspiration
themes.description: Highly curated, visually perfect content (home decor, fashion, art) designed to be aspirational.
themes.psychological_driver: Satisfies the desire for beauty and order. Can be calming but also promotes comparison and dissatisfaction with one's own environment.
warnings: Can set unrealistic standards for appearance and environment.
May promote overconsumption to achieve the 'aesthetic'.
Hides the effort, cost, and privilege behind the curation.

themes.name: Fitness & Transformation
themes.description: Content showing physical transformations, workouts, or 'what I eat in a day' content.
examples: What I Eat in a Day to Lose Weight
themes.psychological_driver: Aspirational but also triggering. Can inspire healthy behavior but also promote body dissatisfaction and comparison.
warnings: Can promote unhealthy body image and eating disorders.
Often unrealistic or unsustainable methods.
May not disclose use of supplements, editing, or other factors.

education_infotainment.name: Education & Infotainment
education_infotainment.description: Content that educates or informs, but in a highly engaging, entertaining format. Can be genuinely valuable but also addictive.

themes.name: Deep Dive / Explainer
themes.description: Long-form video essays or documentary-style content about a specific topic.
themes.psychological_driver: Satisfies curiosity and provides a sense of learning and intellectual stimulation. The long format can lead to 'just one more video' binging.
warnings: Can give a false sense of expertise from passive consumption.
Quality and accuracy vary widely.
Long format can lead to significant time investment.

themes.name: Quick Facts / Trivia
themes.description: Bite-sized, surprising facts or trivia delivered rapidly.
themes.psychological_driver: Provides quick dopamine hits of 'learning' without requiring deep thought. Easy to consume in rapid succession.
warnings: Often lacks context or nuance.
May spread misinformation if not fact-checked.
Promotes shallow learning over deep understanding.

themes.name: How-To / Tutorial
themes.description: Step-by-step instructional content teaching a skill or process.
themes.psychological_driver: Provides a clear path to skill acquisition. Can be genuinely useful but also leads to 'tutorial hell' where consumption replaces action.
warnings: Can lead to passive learning without actual practice.
May oversimplify complex skills.
Viewer may collect tutorials without implementing them.
